stage1.impression: A believable dusk streetscape: the tree, the bark, the dark stone/steel cladding and the warm room glimpsed through the glass all hold up at 1:1, and the lens is honest (level, true verticals, 50 mm). But it reads as late-afternoon overcast, not blue hour or night: the stucco, the white cornice and the sidewalk are brighter than the lit room, so the shopfront does not glow. The frosted lightbox is a dead grey pane with a ghost, the etched name reads as opaque pink vinyl, the upper flats' blinds and cornice are flat CG, and no EARF speaker or tint is legible anywhere. A magazine would see a handsome but generic storefront, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The room behind the glass must be the brightest thing in the frame apart from the street lamps: interior [440,360,740,620] lum_median >= 45 while the upper facade [230,0,1050,235] sits at or below 60
The exterior must read blue hour: cool sky-lit surfaces (b_median >= r_median on the upper facade and the neighbouring stucco) against amber interior light
The frosted lightbox with the dancing silhouette must glow evenly and read at a glance (median 80 to 130), not as a dark grey pane
At least one Atmosphere speaker, lit and showing its smoked tint, must be legible through the glass
The etched name must read as frosted etching on glass, translucent and catching the room light, not as opaque pink letters
The shopfront glass must carry a faint, clean reflection of the street (tree, lamp, far facade), as real plate glass does at dusk
The specific cues (record wall, back bar, Domes) must be readable enough to make this Planet EARF rather than any bar

defects.what: Upper flats: blinds are uniform striped CG panels, white cornice lit evenly from nowhere at lum_median 88.5, brighter than the shop
Neighbouring stucco flat and evenly lit at lum_median 76, warm (r87 b69): daylight, not blue hour; left window's blinds are flat stripes
Right-hand stucco at lum_median 84, brighter than the lit interior
Frosted lightbox dark (lum_median 20.4) with a muddy shadow-figure: reads as a smudge on glass, not a back-lit panel
Etched name opaque and pink (r187 g149 b126, median 155): reads as vinyl signage, not etched glass
Interior through glass at lum_median 27.4 with 0.25% clipped at the pendant: the room is underexposed relative to the street
No EARF speaker or saturated tint legible; the round dark object at about [705,470,740,500] is unreadable
Shopfront glass shows no reflection of the street, tree or lamps: reads as an open hole or matte film
Sidewalk evenly lit (lum_median 68.5) with only faint lamp pools; no night falloff
Entry alcove warm and fine, but the threshold floor at [790,690,960,720] is a flat bright slab

changes.expected: Sky-lit surfaces drop by about 0.8 stop to a median near 50 to 55; the frame median falls from 53.6 to about 35.

changes.problem: Inside, the room is too dim to read as the lit heart of the street once exposure comes down.
